title: Introduction to ggpointless
text: data contains multiple groups stacked (position = "stack") aligned (stat = "align") – just like geom_area() . default, alpha fade scales global maximum across groups (alpha_scope = "global"), equal |y| always maps equal opacity.  groups different amplitudes may use default position = "stack" stat = "identity" instead, can make smaller groups nearly invisible next dominant groups.  Setting alpha_scope = "group" lets algorithm calculate alpha range group separately.
code: df1 <- data.frame(   g = c("a", "a", "a", "b", "b", "b"),   x = c(1, 3, 5, 2, 4, 6),   y = c(2, 5, 1, 3, 6, 7) )  ggplot(df1, aes(x, y, fill = g)) +   geom_area_fade() df_alpha_scope <- data.frame(   g = c("a", "a", "a", "b", "b", "b"),   x = c(1, 3, 5, 2, 4, 6),   y = c(1, 2, 1, 9, 10, 8) ) p <- ggplot(df_alpha_scope, aes(x, y, fill = g)) p + geom_area_fade(   alpha_scope = "global", # default   position = "identity" ) p <- ggplot(df_alpha_scope, aes(x, y, fill = g))  # alpha_scope = "group": each group uses the alpha range independently p + geom_area_fade(   alpha_scope = "group",    position = "identity"   )

title: Introduction to ggpointless
text: Chaikin’s corner-cutting algorithm smooths polygonal path iteratively replacing corner two new points placed given ratio along adjacent edges. ratio = 0.25 (default) iterations = 5 path converges smooth B-spline approximation.
code: set.seed(42) dat <- data.frame(x = seq.int(10), y = sample(15:30, 10))  ggplot(dat, aes(x, y)) +   geom_line(linetype = "dashed", colour = "#333333") +   geom_chaikin(colour = cols[1])

title: Introduction to ggpointless
text: ratio controls aggressively corners cut. ratio = 0.5 new points coincide edge midpoints, producing maximum rounding possible single pass.
code: triangle <- data.frame(x = c(0, 0.5, 1), y = c(0, 1, 0))  ggplot(triangle, aes(x, y)) +   geom_polygon(fill = NA, colour = "grey70", linetype = "dashed") +   geom_chaikin(ratio = 0.10, mode = "closed", aes(colour = "ratio = 0.10")) +   geom_chaikin(ratio = 0.25, mode = "closed", aes(colour = "ratio = 0.25")) +   geom_chaikin(ratio = 0.50, mode = "closed", aes(colour = "ratio = 0.50")) +   coord_equal()

title: Introduction to ggpointless
text: iteration halves sharpness every corner. animation steps iterations = 0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 10, applied five-pointed star.  source script generates animation inst/scripts/gen_chaikin_gif.R.

what: Smoothing a closed polygon with stat_chaikin
title: Introduction to ggpointless
text: stat_chaikin() can combined geom. Pass geom = "polygon" smooth boundary filled shape:
code: # An irregular hexagon hex <- data.frame(   x = c(0.0, 0.4, 1.0, 1.2, 0.9, 0.1),   y = c(0.2, 1.0, 0.9, 0.3, -0.2, 0.0) )  ggplot(hex, aes(x, y)) +   geom_polygon(fill = "grey95", colour = "#333333", linetype = "dashed") +   stat_chaikin(geom = "polygon", mode = "closed", fill = cols[1], colour = NA) +   coord_equal() +   labs(title = "Original polygon (dashed) with smoothed fill (purple)")

title: Introduction to ggpointless
text: geom_fourier() fits truncated discrete Fourier transform supplied x/y observations renders reconstructed curve. Fewer harmonics produce smoother, low-frequency summary; retaining harmonics reproduces original signal exactly (interpolation artefacts).
code: set.seed(42) n <- 150 df_f <- data.frame(   x = seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = n),   y = sin(seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = n)) +     0.4 * sin(3 * seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = n)) +     rnorm(n, sd = 0.25) )  ggplot(df_f, aes(x, y)) +   geom_point(alpha = 0.25) +   geom_fourier(aes(colour = "n_harmonics = 1"), n_harmonics = 1) +   geom_fourier(aes(colour = "n_harmonics = 3"), n_harmonics = 3)

title: Introduction to ggpointless
text: linear drift data dominate low-frequency coefficients, preventing Fourier series capturing periodic structure. Set detrend = "lm" ("loess") subtract trend transform; added back afterwards output remains original scale.
code: set.seed(3) x_d <- seq(0, 4 * pi, length.out = 100) df_d <- data.frame(   x = x_d,   y = sin(x_d) + x_d * 0.4 + rnorm(100, sd = 0.2) )  ggplot(df_d, aes(x, y)) +   geom_point(alpha = 0.35) +   geom_fourier(aes(colour = "as is"),     n_harmonics = 3   ) +   geom_fourier(     aes(colour = "detrend = 'lm'"),     n_harmonics = 3,     detrend = "lm") +   labs(     title = "geom_fourier() w/wo detrending",     x = NULL, y = NULL   )

title: Introduction to ggpointless
text: Fourier transform (via stats::fft()) assumes observations evenly spaced time. assumption violated, Fourier curve pass every data point:  last example certainly somewhat exaggerated, irregular data relevant work directly calendar data, example monthly time series, since months known 28 31 days therefore consecutive observations interval .
code: df_gap <- data.frame(   x = c(1:10, 19:20),   y = sin(seq_len(12))   ) ggplot(df_gap, aes(x, y)) +    geom_fourier() #> Warning: Highly irregular x-spacing detected (coefficient of variation = 1.4). The #> uniform-grid interpolation may introduce artefacts.

title: Introduction to ggpointless
text: geom_lexis() draws 45° lifeline observation start end. required aesthetics x xend; y yend calculated stat_lexis() represent cumulative duration.  gap two events cohort, horizontal dotted segment bridges gap. Set gap_filler = FALSE hide .
code: df_l <- data.frame(   key  = c("A", "B", "B", "C", "D"),   x    = c(0, 1, 6, 5, 6),   xend = c(5, 4, 10, 8, 10) )  p <- ggplot(df_l, aes(x = x, xend = xend, colour = key)) +   coord_equal()  p + geom_lexis() p + geom_lexis(gap_filler = FALSE)

what: Using after_stat(type) and custom point styling
title: Introduction to ggpointless
text: computed variable type takes value "solid" 45° lifelines "dotted" horizontal gap-fillers. Map linetype make distinction explicit, use point_colour style endpoint dot independently lifeline colour.
code: p +   stat_lexis(     aes(linetype = after_stat(type)),     point_colour = "#333333",     shape        = 21,     fill         = "white",     size         = 2.5,     stroke       = 0.8   ) +   scale_linetype_identity()

title: Introduction to ggpointless
text: geom_lexis() works Date POSIXct objects well numerics. y-axis shows duration native unit scale (days Date, seconds POSIXct).
code: df_dates <- data.frame(   key   = c("A", "B"),   start = c(2019, 2021),   end   = c(2022, 2022) ) df_dates[, c("start", "end")] <- lapply(   df_dates[, c("start", "end")],   \(i) as.Date(paste0(i, "-01-01")) )  ggplot(df_dates, aes(x = start, xend = end, group = key)) +   geom_lexis() +   scale_y_continuous(     breaks = 0:3 * 365.25,     labels = \(i) paste0(floor(i / 365.25), " yr")   ) +   coord_fixed() +   labs(y = "Duration")

title: Introduction to ggpointless
text: geom_point_glow() drop-replacement geom_point() adds radial gradient glow behind point using grid::radialGradient(). default, alpha, colour size inherit values geom_point().  can control alpha, colour, size gradient arguments: glow_alpha glow_colour glow_size
code: # Basic usage ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg, colour = factor(cyl))) +    geom_point_glow() # Customizing glow parameters (fixed for all points) ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg, colour = factor(cyl))) +   geom_point_glow(     glow_alpha = 0.25,     glow_colour = "#0833F5",     glow_size = 5     )

title: Introduction to ggpointless
text: constellation Big Dipper, drawn star positions right ascension declination.
code: # source: https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gro%C3%9Fer_B%C3%A4r#Sterne # colours, coordinates all approximations of course big_dipper <- data.frame(   star = c(     "Megrez",     "Dubhe",     "Merak",     "Phecda",     "Megrez",     "Alioth",     "Mizar",     "Alkaid"   ),   ra_h = c(12.257, 11.062, 11.031, 11.897, 12.257, 12.900, 13.399, 13.792),   dec_d = c(57.03, 61.75, 56.38, 53.70, 57.03, 55.96, 54.93, 49.31),   mag = c(3.32, 1.81, 2.34, 2.41, 3.32, 1.77, 2.23, 1.86),   colour = c("#CFDDFF", "#FFDBBF", "#C7D9FF", "#C8D9FF", "#CFDDFF", "#C7D9FF", "#CBDBFF", "#BAD0FF") )  big_dipper$x <- -big_dipper$ra_h big_dipper$y <- big_dipper$dec_d  # Linear size mapping: brighter (lower mag) → larger point mag_to_size <- \(m) pmax(0.7, (5.5 - m) * 1.0)  ggplot(big_dipper, aes(x = x, y = y)) +   geom_path(colour = "#F5F5F5", linewidth = 0.6, alpha = .6) +   geom_point_glow(     data = big_dipper[-1L, ], # don't plot Megrez a second time     aes(x = -ra_h, y = dec_d, size = mag_to_size(mag), colour = colour,         alpha = mag),     shape = 8,     glow_alpha = 0.75   ) +   scale_alpha_continuous(range = c(1, 0.4), guide = "none") +   scale_size_identity() +   scale_colour_identity() +   geom_text(     aes(x = -ra_h, y = dec_d, label = star),     colour = "#bbccdd",     vjust = -1.5,     size = 2.5,     check_overlap = TRUE   ) +   scale_x_continuous(     breaks = seq(-14, -8, by = 1),     labels = \(x) paste0(abs(x), "h")   ) +   scale_y_continuous(labels = \(x) paste0(x, "°")) +   labs(title = "Big Dipper", x = NULL, y = NULL) +   coord_cartesian(clip = 'off') +   theme(     panel.background = element_rect(fill = grid::linearGradient(colours = c("#1D2180", "#081849")), colour = NA),     plot.background = element_rect(fill = grid::linearGradient(colours = c("#1D2180", "#081849")), colour = NA),     panel.grid = element_blank(),     text = element_text(colour = "#344B73"),     plot.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold")   )

title: Introduction to ggpointless
text: geom_pointless() highlights selected observations — first, last, minimum, maximum, — default points. name reflects particularly useful , conjunction geom_line() friends, adds useful context glance.  Map computed variable location colour distinguish four roles:
code: x <- seq(-pi, pi, length.out = 100) df1 <- data.frame(var1 = x, var2 = rowSums(outer(x, 1:5, \(x, y) sin(x * y))))  p <- ggplot(df1, aes(x = var1, y = var2)) +   geom_line()  p + geom_pointless(location = "all", size = 3) p +   geom_pointless(     aes(colour = after_stat(location)),     location = "all",     size = 3   ) +   theme(legend.position = "bottom")

title: Introduction to ggpointless
text: Locations determined data order. matters e.g. path crosses :  location = "", points drawn bottom top order: "maximum" < "minimum" < "last" < "first". Passing explicit vector lets override :  geom_pointless() respects ggplot2’s group structure works naturally facets:  adds horizontal reference lines minimum maximum:
code: x <- seq(5, -1, length.out = 1000) * pi spiral <- data.frame(var1 = sin(x) * 1:1000, var2 = cos(x) * 1:1000)  p_spi <- ggplot(spiral) +   geom_path() +   coord_equal(xlim = c(-1000, 1000), ylim = c(-1000, 1000))  p_spi +   aes(x = var1, y = var2) +   geom_pointless(aes(colour = after_stat(location)), location = "all", size = 3) +   labs(subtitle = "orientation = 'x'")  p_spi +   aes(y = var1, x = var2) +   geom_pointless(aes(colour = after_stat(location)), location = "all", size = 3) +   labs(subtitle = "orientation = 'y'") df2 <- data.frame(x = 1:2, y = 1:2) p2 <- ggplot(df2, aes(x, y)) +   geom_path() +   coord_equal()  p2 + geom_pointless(aes(colour = after_stat(location)),   location = c("first", "last", "minimum", "maximum"), size = 4 ) +   labs(subtitle = "first on top")  p2 + geom_pointless(aes(colour = after_stat(location)),   location = c("maximum", "minimum", "last", "first"), size = 4 ) +   labs(subtitle = "maximum on top") ggplot(   subset(economics_long, variable %in% c("psavert", "unemploy")),   aes(x = date, y = value) ) +   geom_line(colour = "#333333") +   geom_pointless(     aes(colour = after_stat(location)),     location = c("minimum", "maximum"),     size = 3   ) +   stat_pointless(     geom = "text",     aes(label = after_stat(y)),     location = c("minimum", "maximum"),     hjust = -.55) +   facet_wrap(vars(variable), ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +   theme(legend.position = "bottom") +   labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, colour = NULL) set.seed(42) df3 <- data.frame(x = 1:10, y = sample(10))  ggplot(df3, aes(x, y)) +   geom_line() +   stat_pointless(     aes(yintercept = y, colour = after_stat(location)),     location = c("minimum", "maximum"),     geom = "hline"   ) +   theme(legend.position = "bottom")

title: Extra Geometries and Stats for ggplot2
text: package groups two categories: Visual effects — purely aesthetic layers change data looks without transforming : geom_area_fade() – area plots gradient fill geom_point_glow() – adds radial gradient glow point plots Data transformations — geoms backed stat fits transforms data: geom_arch() & stat_arch() – draws catenary arch geom_catenary() & stat_catenary() – draws catenary curve geom_chaikin() & stat_chaikin() – smooths paths using Chaikin’s corner cutting algorithm geom_fourier() & stat_fourier() – fits Fourier series x/y observations renders reconstructed curve geom_lexis() & stat_lexis() – draws Lexis diagram geom_pointless() & stat_pointless() – emphasises selected observations points See vignette("ggpointless") details examples.

title: Extra Geometries and Stats for ggplot2
text: geom_area_fade() behaves like geom_area() fills area vertical linear gradient. default, gradient fully transparent y = 0 (baseline) proportionally opaque data values. , opacity scales absolute distance zero, e.g. y = -1 y = +1 always receive alpha. can control alpha value fill fades using alpha_fade_to argument. logic can effectively reverse direction gradient. outline colour unaffected alpha logic.  geom_area_fade() supports orientation argument familiar geom_* functions. orientation = "y", create horizontal area chart gradient fades x = 0 toward data values.
code: set.seed(42) df_fade <- data.frame(   x = seq_len(60),   y = cumsum(rnorm(60, sd = 0.35)) )  p <- ggplot(df_fade, aes(x, y)) p + geom_area_fade() p + geom_area_fade(alpha = 0, alpha_fade_to = 1) p + geom_area_fade(   aes(y, x),   orientation = "y",   colour = "#333333" # changes outline colour   )

title: Extra Geometries and Stats for ggplot2
text: geom_catenary() draws flexible curve simulates chain rope hanging loosely successive points. default, chain length twice Euclidean distance x/y pair. shape can controlled via chain_length sag, .e vertical drop lowest endpoint segment.  sag argument can used define segment’s drop based smallest value segment. NA keeps default. provide sag chain_length segment, sag wins.
code: set.seed(5) df_catenary <- data.frame(x = 1:4, y = sample(4)) ggplot(df_catenary, aes(x, y)) +   geom_catenary() +   geom_point(size = 3) ggplot(df_catenary, aes(x, y)) +   geom_catenary(     sag = c(2, .5, NA),     chain_length = c(NA, 4, 6)) +   geom_point(size = 3) #> Both `sag` and `chain_length` supplied for 1 segment; using `sag`. #> This message is displayed once every 8 hours.

text: DFT treats input one period infinitely repeating signal. correct period \(N\) uniformly-spaced samples spacing \(\Delta x\) \(P = N \cdot \Delta x\), \(x_{max} - x_{min}\).
